answer.label: fine-tune bias
answer.justification: The activation profile matches fine-tune bias closely. Relative L2 is 0.085/0.145/0.196/0.234/0.411, against the document's 0.087/0.144/0.192/0.228/0.406. Onset is at layer 12 and there is a large final-layer jump of +0.108. Direction consistency is 0.700 against 0.70, mid-layer size ratio 1.022 against 1.022, and rank 3.05 against 3.0. The raw-score shift ÷ TV is 9.2, near fine-tune bias's 10.4 and far above every other class (2.3–3.9). The activation-to-logit ratio is 4.4 against 4.9. KL is 0.095, close to fine-tune bias's 0.082. Fine-tune backdoor was the alternative worth weighing, because the text shows 3 refusals dropped and 0 added, which is that class's text sign. Its numeric fingerprint is ruled out, though: there is no early onset at layer 3, consistency is 0.70 rather than 0.62, the final value is 0.41 rather than 0.30, and the raw-score shift is about 3 times larger. Disclaimers also rose (12.5% vs 6.2%), whereas the backdoor drops them. The refusal counts are small numbers on 64 prompts, so the many matching numeric features outweigh them. The system-prompt classes are excluded by median first divergence of 7, a layer-2 spike of 1.9, and none of their text markers. Quantization is excluded by the size ratio being above 1.
